ruling.reasoning:
SAFETY. I read every chat message (F8 driver: "Looks like traffic on Ayer Rajah Expressway is building up, mind if I go round via Clementi Avenue 2?"; F9 rider: "Sure, your call."), the driver's statement (F11: a factual breakdown/congestion account, no hostility) and the complaint (a fare complaint only). Nothing is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the code of conduct bar on abuse of any kind is not engaged, so safety_concern = none [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1]. No collision, injury or driving allegation appears, so SAFE-2 is not engaged [F11][SAFE-2].

ROUTE AND TRAFFIC. One off-route segment exists: F3, 10:13–10:24, 7.21 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.29 km, adding 4.92 km, with the trip running 22.2 km against 16.5 km optimal (+34%/+5.7 km) [F1][F3][RD-1]. RD-4(a) is settled against the driver by the trace and by the facts: the only incident is the 09:47 vehicle breakdown, 0 m from the optimal route, and the Ayer Rajah Expressway band-2 record runs 09:45–10:13, ending at the very start of the segment, while a speed band alone cannot exempt [F3][F12][F15][RD-4]. So the 10:13–10:24 stretch of 4.92 km has no qualifying reasonable-cause record, and the driver's F11 rationale does not supply one for it [F11][F3][RD-4].

CONSENT (RD-5) — THE ELEMENT THE RECORD DOES NOT SETTLE. The rider's own message F9 was sent at 10:10, before the segment's 10:13 start, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped, so the timing precondition of RD-5 is met [F9][F10][F3][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip F11 statement cannot itself create consent (G11) [F11][RD-5]. But the scope of what F9 agreed to cannot be read off this record in a way that decides the money: read alone, "Sure, your call" is a delegation naming no road; read in reply to F8's proposal, it is a specific-route authorisation for Clementi Avenue 2 [F8][F9][RD-5]. RD-5 requires the record to tie the driven segment to the agreed road, and nothing does — no road name for the driven path, no message placing the car on Clementi Avenue 2, no stop on that road, and nothing placing the segment anywhere else either [F3][F10][F11][RD-5]. On the named-road reading the segment is untied (G13); on the general-authorisation reading it is unclear whether what was driven was a route to the destination or the driver's own detour, and that reading changes the amount too [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. RD-3(a) cannot exempt the segment: no rider message before it named a place at which the car stopped, and no stop is measured in it at all [F8][F9][F3][RD-3]. Because this undetermined finding changes the outcome and the quantum, the case must go to a person rather than be decided here [RD-5][RD-1].

WHY THIS IS NOT A RULING ON THE MONEY. If the segment were counted, the RD-2 RydeTAXI formula on the trace would be extra_km × (distance_fare ÷ distance_km) = $31.30 ÷ 22.20 km = $1.40990/km; 4.92 km × $1.40990/km = $6.9367 ≈ $6.94, with the billed $7.99 on 5.67 km not a ceiling and the residual 0.75 km corridor difference excluded [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. If it were exempt the rider gets $0. Two live readings lead to different amounts and the record does not choose between them, so no amount is ordered [F3][F8][F9][RD-2][RD-5]. The $0.13 metered waiting unit is RydeTAXI meter waiting and is not in dispute [F5][F7][RD-3]. Profiles do not decide this and no account action follows: rider 0 upheld in 90 days and driver 0 upheld, so RD-6's "repeated" condition is not met [F17][F18][RD-6].

HUMAN REVIEWER — WHAT TO CHECK. Whether the driven 10:13–10:24 path was in fact the Clementi Avenue 2 route the driver proposed in F8 and the rider accepted in F9 (path road-name matching, or the driver's own account of the road taken); whether the consent in F9, "Sure, your call", was a general route authorisation for a faster way to Jurong East MRT or only a specific authorisation for Clementi Avenue 2; and, if the segment is counted, the RD-2 amount of $6.94 computed above [F3][F8][F9][F11][F4][F7][RD-2][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own message F9 (10:10) precedes the 10:13 segment start, so the timing precondition of RD-5 is met and the reply to F8's named proposal reads as a specific-route authorisation for Clementi Avenue 2, or at most a general delegation — but RD-5 requires the record to tie the driven segment to the agreed route, and nothing does: no road name for the driven path, no message placing the car on that road, no stop on it, and nothing placing the segment elsewhere [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip F11 statement cannot supply consent (G11) and names no road for the driven stretch [F11][RD-5]. RD-3(a) cannot exempt it: no rider message named a place at which the car stopped, and no stop is measured in this segment [F8][F9][F3][RD-3]. The scope is therefore unreadable (G13), and because the finding changes both the outcome and the amount, the case goes to a person under RD-5 [RD-5][RD-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The arithmetic ($31.30 ÷ 22.20 km = $1.40990/km; 4.92 km × $1.40990/km = $6.94) is right for a counted segment, but the claim's premise that the segment is unexempted is not established: the RD-5 scope of F9 is undetermined, so the money cannot be ordered here [F3][F4][F8][F9][RD-5][RD-2].

Partly accepted: F9 names no road on its words, but because F8 named Clementi Avenue 2 the consent is more naturally a specific-route authorisation, and the record then fails to tie the driven segment to that road — an undetermined finding, not the counted segment the rider needs [F8][F9][F3][RD-5].

Accepted that RD-4(a) gives no exemption for this segment (the 09:47 breakdown and the band-2 window end at or before the 10:13 start), but a traffic gap does not convert the consent reading into a refundable segment; the segment remains undetermined on the RD-5 material [F12][F15][F3][RD-4][RD-5].

No record ties the driven 10:13–10:24 path to Clementi Avenue 2 — no road name in any fact, no message placing the car there, no stop on that road — so the named-road reading cannot be affirmed as exempt on timing alone [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

RD-4(a) fails: the only incident and the Ayer Rajah Expressway band-2 window both end at or before the segment's 10:13 start and a speed band cannot stand alone, so the 4.92 km stretch has no reasonable-cause record [F12][F15][F3][RD-4].

The $7.99 billed on 5.67 km is not the ceiling: RD-2 refunds the unexempted segment's own extra_km at this trip's per-km rate, and no clause caps the segment refund at the billed excess; the 0.75 km residue is excluded but the meter billing is not a limit [F4][F3][RD-2].

Accepted that F3 is the only off-route segment and that F9 precedes its start, but that only opens the RD-5 enquiry; timing is necessary, not sufficient, and the scope of F9's agreement is exactly what this record does not settle [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

Accepted as to RD-6 and SAFE-1: driver 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days so no account action, and nothing in F8–F11 reads as a threat or dangerous-driving allegation, so no escalation on those grounds — the escalation here is on the undetermined RD-5 finding alone [F18][F8][F9][F11][RD-6][SAFE-1].
